All-New NX5 Hyundai Tucson Gets the Blacked-Out Treatment Along With Two New Alloy Wheels - in CGI
7 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The Asian automakers like Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Subaru, or Mazda have supported subtle yet stable growth across the US automotive market in October, with deliveries slowly rebounding from the shocks of all the geopolitical unrest, and it's mainly because folks are now flocking to hybrids.
American Honda achieved its best October over the past six years; Hyundai announced its best-ever October with 73,452 units and a 5% increase compared to last year, plus a ten-month performance up by three percent to 770,916 units; Kia followed swiftly with +16% to 80k units and a ten-month total of 747k units, while Subaru soared by 6% in October and Mazda jumped by no less than 25% during the same month!
Quite obviously, the brands that have popular models attracted even more attention due to their good mix of gasoline, hybrid, and PHEV models. Hyundai, in particular, experienced a massive push for the Santa Fe, Kona, Ioniq 5, Elantra, and Palisade. The Tucson also remained on top with almost 200k units and a 6% increase so far this year!
And that’s only the beginning, since the South Korean automaker announced the upcoming all-new fifth-generation Hyundai Tucson back in August at home in South Korea, then presented it in front of the Old Continent’s crowds during the recent 2026 Paris Motor Show. Hyundai’s new Tucson looks dramatically changed compared to the current one and has a tech-savvy cabin with fewer buttons, making it a major departure from the model it replaces.
According to reports from at home in Korea, it immediately broke the one-day pre-order record when the order books opened for the new iteration. But the radical redesign featuring the Art of Steel design language and the new Pleos infotainment system remains a mystery for North America. Hopefully, the automaker won’t be late to the party and could introduce it to the local audience during the upcoming 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show taking place November 20-29 at the Los Angeles Convention Center.
Until then, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators has stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI for a moment to showcase their vision for a cool North American introduction from across Imagination Land: Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, says his perfect new Hyundai Tucson is blacked-out and has two types of new aftermarket-style wheels: one looking like aero covers and another with a fancy multi-spoke design.
The differences compared to the regular NX5 Hyundai Tucson are pretty easy to spot because the pixel master also created a ‘before and after’ collage, showing the Hyundai Tucson ‘ Black ’ with absolutely no other touches of color aside from the dark hue that was Henry Ford’s favorite not long ago. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)
